en.title: Fresh snow in the Alps: 21 cm in 72 hours at Kope (3 November)
en.description: Kope got 21 cm of new snow in the last 72 hours. It now has about 11 cm on its upper slopes, according to our snow model.
en.lede: Kope got 21 cm of new snow in the last 72 hours. It now has about 11 cm on its upper slopes, according to our snow model.

p: Elsewhere, Lackenhof, Rogla and Trije Kralji got 18 cm, 17 cm and 17 cm in the last 72 hours.
Our snow model shows 25,190 km² of snow-covered ground in the Alps today, with snow at 584 of 1,178 resorts.
On Friday 6 November the freezing level climbs to about 2,980 m, above the top of the lifts at 1,535 m: rain can fall even at the top.
Rain on fresh snow makes it heavy and, after a cold night, icy: the days after are better for groomed runs than for powder.
At about 1,120 m, Kope has 5 cm today; a normal 3 November has 0 cm there.
That is more than in 44 of the 46 past winters on this date.
In past winters the best snow at Kope usually came mid-February / late February.
Day by day at Kope: Tuesday 3 November 2 cm; Wednesday 4 November 2 cm.
Height by height at Kope: 705 m 0 cm on the ground, 0 cm more in the next 7 days; 1,120 m 1 cm on the ground, 0 cm more in the next 7 days; 1,535 m 6 cm on the ground, 2 cm more in the next 7 days.

The Schönbüel station (1,777 m) measured 14 cm of snow on the ground on 2 November, with 11 cm of new snow in 24 hours. The Feuerkogel station (1,618 m) measured 9 cm of snow on the ground on 1 November, with 9 cm of new snow in 24 hours. The Plattkopf station (2,220 m) measured 30 cm of snow on the ground on 2 November, with 8 cm of new snow in 24 hours.
Keep in mind: resort values come from our snow model and describe an area, while stations measure one point.
Height matters: at Kope, our model gives 6 cm at the top (1,535 m), 1 cm at mid-mountain (1,120 m) and 0 cm at the base (705 m).
At Kope, the freezing level reaches 2,810 m to 2,980 m on 6 November, above the top of the resort (1,535 m): rain or wet snow is possible on every slope that day.
Until 6 November, our forecast gives 3 cm at Rogla, 2 cm at Kope and 2 cm at Trije Kralji.
Forecasts a few days ahead can change: look at the map again the day before you travel.
After fresh snow, wind builds drifts on sheltered slopes. Off-piste, the first days after a snowfall need the most care.

advice: Fresh snow is best in the first hours after it stops: go early, before the sun and the crowds.
Look for snow high up and on north-facing slopes: they keep it longest, while south-facing slopes lose it first in the sun.
Before you ski off-piste or go touring, read the official avalanche bulletin (links below).
Snow on the map does not mean a resort is open: check lifts and opening dates on the resort's website.
Get a powder alert in the SnowScope app to know when Kope gets fresh snow.
